title: Best force is no force
article: A letter from Mike Welsby, Duncan.

A prime consideration in the probe of tasers must be the use of force by our local police departments. Most disciplined policing and peacekeeping forces throughout the world employ the "escalating force" principle, which applies a suitable amount of resistance/ action to remedy a given situation.

I would like to forward for consideration another force option that I have seen used during peacekeeping operations to great effect, but which is apparently not in vogue with our own police forces: The use of no force. By this, I do not mean doing nothing, or letting a dangerous situation escalate. By using no force, I mean cordoning off an area and allowing the difficult situation to play out until a more safe and suitable option is available for use.

How could this method have been employed in the situation of Robert Bagnell, who was killed with a taser? Bagnell had locked himself in a hotel bathroom and was screaming and destroying things. So what! He was of no immediate danger to anyone. The use of no force would have tied up a police team for a while, but would have saved a life, much money and police time in the end. Same with Majensio Camaso, another local taser victim.

With regard to force, a taser is preferred to using the gun. Pepper spray is gentler than a taser, but using no force at all can save a lot of pain, litigation and suggests a controlled, compassionate police force.
